start.text: A silvered post with a crossbar of iron hooks. On the hooks: a child's shoe on its lace, a faded ribbon, a key on a string, a bundle of letters tied up, a spoon, and on the fifth hook a little wooden gull, wings out, turning slowly though there's no wind.
At its foot, a heap of things nobody took: a cap, a cup, a rag doll, all gone the colour of the fog.

word_left.text: Your strip of sailcloth is still knotted under the bar, the red cord through it. Nobody has taken it. Nobody has let it go grey, either.

nothing_left.text: You left nothing here. The gull turns on its thread.

leave.text: Hesper said: hang it there. If they want it, it goes. If they don't, the fog has it.

choice.text: Tie on Mara's word: the stool's still by the door.
Tie on word of your own: someone from Saltmarrow came looking.
Leave nothing. He came here to put things down.

tie_mara.text: You knot a strip of sailcloth under the bar and thread a red cord through it. Nobody here reads, so you say it to the post, low: the stool's still by the door. Don't tell him to come home. He knows where it is.
It feels like nothing. It feels like setting out a cup.

tie_own.text: You knot a strip of sailcloth under the bar and thread a red cord through it, and say it to the post, low: someone from Saltmarrow came looking. Somebody remembers you.

leave_nothing.text: You let your hand fall. The gull on its thread turns its back to you, and then its face, and then its back.
